stories.title: US peace envoys Witkoff and Kushner believed to have arrived in Moscow
stories.summary: The announcement came as Russian strikes on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed four overnight, per local authorities. US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are believed to have arrived in Russia ahead of meetings with officials from Moscow and Kyiv this weekend. The pair come armed with a "proposal to end the war," US President Donald Trump has announced, as the US makes its latest push to break a diplomatic deadlock over the war in Ukraine. "I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we'll do it," Trump told reporters on Friday. The duo is then due to head to Kyiv on Sunday, in what will be their first visits to the Ukrainian capital since Trump returned to the White house in January last year. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the planned visit to Ukraine in a post on X. "We need to look for real options for how to move this war toward an end," Zelenskyy wrote. "We will see what proposals Steve and Jared bring and what they are told in Moscow in response". He added that Ukrainian forces would ensure the "normal functioning of Russian airspace" to ensure the envoys could make the trip to Moscow safely. Zelenskyy had warned airlines and insurers on Tuesday that Russian airspace would "effectively be closing" due to the scale of Ukrainian drone operations making flying unsafe.

stories.title: Chinese man, Nepali woman found alive 10 days after flood
stories.summary: Rescuers pulled out a 64-year-old Nepali woman alive on Saturday from her home, buried under thick mud and debris when the region was struck by massive flooding 10 days ago, killing over 1,300 people and leaving at least 5,500 missing. Emergency personnel said earlier they had rescued a Chinese man, named only as Luhaitao, found alive inside a 225-metre tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal’s Rasuwa district. stories.title: Masked men block traffic at UK’s Dover port amid anti-immigrant tensions
stories.summary: A group of masked men blocked the entrance to Britain’s busiest ferry port in Dover, bringing traffic to a standstill as police responded to what they called an ongoing public order incident. The protest caused a 6.4-kilometre traffic jam and came amid renewed tensions over immigration and Channel migrant crossings.

stories.title: Flourishing green communities are changing lives
stories.summary: Four projects have been nominated in the environmental category in BBC Radio Devon's Make a Difference Awards. The Growing Well Garden in Bow, the Sampford Peverell Tree Wardens in mid-Devon, Shallowford Farm on Dartmoor, and Sustainable Hatherleigh are being recognised for making their communities more eco-friendly, wilder and healthier. They are doing this in a range of ways from planting trees and growing vegetables, to leading bug hunts and rediscovering nature. The winners of the Make a Difference awards are due to be announced on 24 September at Buckfast Abbey. Growing Well Garden is part of a green social prescribing project, where gardening is used as a therapeutic tool and helps a doctor connect with her patients in a different way. Dr Susan Taheri is an NHS GP at Bow Medical Practice and the founder of Growing Well Garden project - she said the scheme reignited her passion for being a GP. She said meeting patients in a garden can have benefits compared to seeing them a consulting room and describes the garden as her "happy place". "There's a lot more getting your hands dirty and not worrying too much about germs," she said. Shallowford Farm in the heart of Dartmoor aims to make rural life accessible. Retired horticulturalist Charles Staniland's love for the outdoors started in early childhood and he now volunteers there, teaching young people to get their hands dirty. He said he wanted to show a more physical approach to food, that it doesn't just show up on a plate, and that it's something they can contribute to. Staniland hopes the project can "encourage a new generation to understand and value the world around them".
